Until v4.28.0, I relied a lot on grind being able to "see through" definitional equalities of instance fields to discharge many goals. However, since v4.29.0, grind is no longer be able to identify two definitionally-equal terms in the example below.

  1. How can I make it work again?
  2. Is this considered "defeq abuse"? If so, is there a better design to state intermediate definitions and theorems about them?

Thanks!

inductive Expr where
  | char (c : Char)
  | split (e₁ e₂ : Expr)

inductive Node where
  | char (c : Char) (next : Nat)
  | split (next₁ next₂ : Nat)

def pushExpr (expr : Expr) (next : Nat) (nodes : Array Node) : Array Node :=
  match expr with
  | .char c => nodes.push (Node.char c next)
  | .split e₁ e₂ =>
    let nodes₁ := pushExpr e₁ next nodes
    let nodes₂ := pushExpr e₂ next nodes₁
    nodes₂.push (Node.split nodes₁.size nodes₂.size)

#check pushExpr.induct_unfolding

class ProofData where
  -- The arguments to pushExpr
  expr : Expr
  next : Nat
  nodes : Array Node

namespace ProofData

class PdChar extends ProofData where
  c : Char
  expr_eq : expr = .char c

class PdSplit extends ProofData where
  e₁ : Expr
  e₂ : Expr
  expr_eq : expr = .split e₁ e₂

namespace PdSplit

variable [PdSplit]

@[implicit_reducible, grind =] -- for v4.29.0
-- @[grind =] -- for v4.28.0
def intro (e₁ e₂ : Expr) (next : Nat) (nodes : Array Node) : PdSplit :=
  { expr := .split e₁ e₂, next, nodes, e₁, e₂, expr_eq := rfl }

-- We can state the intermediate `let` variables
@[grind =]
def nodes₁ : Array Node := pushExpr e₁ next nodes
def nodes₂ : Array Node := pushExpr e₂ next nodes₁

-- We can prove theorems about these intermediate variables
theorem lt_nodes₁_size : nodes.size < nodes₁.size := sorry
theorem lt_nodes₂_size : nodes₁.size < nodes₂.size := sorry

end PdSplit

end ProofData

example (e : Expr) (next : Nat) (nodes : Array Node) (i : Nat) (h : i < nodes.size) :
  (pushExpr e next nodes)[i]? = .some nodes[i] := by
  fun_induction pushExpr e next nodes
  next nodes c => sorry
  next nodes e₁ e₂ nodes₁ nodes₂ ih₁ ih₂ =>
    open ProofData PdSplit in
    let pd := PdSplit.intro e₁ e₂ next nodes

    -- These are definitionally equal
    -- have : nodes₁ = pd.nodes₁ := rfl

    -- But grind no longer "see through" the defeq
    have : nodes₁ = pd.nodes₁ := by grind
    sorry

(working v4.28.0 link)
Note: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false didn't fix the issue
Sorry, I'm not sure I follow. I'm seeing this issue while updating to v4.29.0 (but the linked message seems to be about v4.30.0).

It appears the issue is limited to field projections of classes. Replacing class with structure allows grind to determine that the projection gives the same value.

inductive Expr where
  | char (c : Char)
  | split (e₁ e₂ : Expr)

inductive Node where
  | char (c : Char) (next : Nat)
  | split (next₁ next₂ : Nat)

def pushExpr (expr : Expr) (next : Nat) (nodes : Array Node) : Array Node :=
  match expr with
  | .char c => nodes.push (Node.char c next)
  | .split e₁ e₂ =>
    let nodes₁ := pushExpr e₁ next nodes
    let nodes₂ := pushExpr e₂ next nodes₁
    nodes₂.push (Node.split nodes₁.size nodes₂.size)

#check pushExpr.induct_unfolding

structure ProofData where
  -- The arguments to pushExpr
  expr : Expr
  next : Nat
  nodes : Array Node

namespace ProofData

structure PdChar extends ProofData where
  c : Char
  expr_eq : expr = .char c

structure PdSplit extends ProofData where
  e₁ : Expr
  e₂ : Expr
  expr_eq : expr = .split e₁ e₂

namespace PdSplit

variable (pd : PdSplit)

@[implicit_reducible, grind =] -- for v4.29.0
-- @[grind =] -- for v4.28.0
def intro (e₁ e₂ : Expr) (next : Nat) (nodes : Array Node) : PdSplit :=
  { expr := .split e₁ e₂, next, nodes, e₁, e₂, expr_eq := rfl }

-- We can state the intermediate `let` variables
@[grind =]
def nodes₁ : Array Node := pushExpr pd.e₁ pd.next pd.nodes
def nodes₂ : Array Node := pushExpr pd.e₂ pd.next pd.nodes₁

-- We can prove theorems about these intermediate variables
theorem lt_nodes₁_size : pd.nodes.size < pd.nodes₁.size := sorry
theorem lt_nodes₂_size : pd.nodes₁.size < pd.nodes₂.size := sorry

end PdSplit

end ProofData

example (e : Expr) (next : Nat) (nodes : Array Node) (i : Nat) (h : i < nodes.size) :
  (pushExpr e next nodes)[i]? = .some nodes[i] := by
  fun_induction pushExpr e next nodes
  next nodes c => sorry
  next nodes e₁ e₂ nodes₁ nodes₂ ih₁ ih₂ =>
    open ProofData PdSplit in
    let pd := PdSplit.intro e₁ e₂ next nodes

    have : nodes = pd.nodes := by grind

    -- grind can see the definitional equality with structure
    have : nodes₁ = pd.nodes₁ := by grind
    sorry
I haven't had time to look at your example, but perhaps you could try making a minimal example showing the different between structure and class behaviour here? That would be good to understand.

Thanks! Here is a minimal example of the difference

structure S where
  v : Nat

class C where
  v : Nat

example : True := by
  let v := 10
  let s : S := { v := v }
  have : v = s.v := by grind -- succeeds
  sorry

example : True := by
  let v := 10
  let c : C := { v := v }
  have : v = c.v := by grind -- fails
  sorry

I suppose that makes sense:

structure S where
  v : Nat

class C where
  v : Nat

example : True := by
  let v := 10
  let s : S := { v := v }
  have : v = s.v := by with_reducible rfl -- succeeds
  sorry

example : True := by
  let v := 10
  let c : C := { v := v }
  have : v = c.v := by with_reducible rfl --fails
  sorry

And your example works if you add

attribute [grind] C.v

Thanks. The grind attribute was not enough in my case, but I was able to introduce the necessary equalities into the local context using with_reducible_and_instances rfl (example if you want to see).

I'm also noting down here some weird behavior changes in rw/simp I found, but I'm not sure if they are related.

Type simp lemma prevents other simp lemmas from applying

I use a bundled design to abstract some operations, and I saw that it was negatively affected by changes in simp in v4.29.0.

Minimal example

Until v4.28.0, simp was able to apply List.mem_append at h, but in v4.29.0, c₁_t prevents it from applying. Removing c₁_t from the simp set could work around the issue in this case, but it also made simp somewhat weaker, such as being unable to discharge none = none in other places (I couldn't minimize this one).

structure C where
  T : Type

def C₁ : C where
  T := List Nat

@[simp] -- Removing this from simpset makes the following pass in v4.29.0
theorem c₁_t : C₁.T = List Nat := rfl

example {s₁ s₂ : List C₁.T} {x : C₁.T} (h : x ∈ s₁ ++ s₂) : True := by
  simp at h
  have should_pass : x ∈ s₁ ∨ x ∈ s₂ := h
  sorry

rw cannot rewrite seemingly equal, definitely defeq expression

I found that some rw invocations that worked in v4.28.0 no longer work in v4.29.0

Not Minimal Example

Taken from here. I have no idea how I can minimize this.

A weird thing is that the rewriting theorem and the local hypothesis to be rewritten looks identical in InfoView (as it applied before). Moreover, just restating the local hypothesis verbatim from the InfoView, which passes as defeq, makes rw work again. So I guess there is something that makes them not equal from the view of rw, but I don't know how to debug from here. Any suggestions are appreciated!

-- local context:
-- h : Regex.VM.εClosure (BufferStrategy s bufferSize) nfa wf pos matchedB nextB ((materializeUpdates bufferSize update, state') :: stack'.materialize) = resultB

-- rw [rewriteTheorem otherLemma] at h -- doesn't work

-- Restate h verbatim
have h : Regex.VM.εClosure (BufferStrategy s bufferSize) nfa wf pos matchedB nextB ((materializeUpdates bufferSize update, state') :: stack'.materialize) = resultB := h
rw [rewriteTheorem otherLemma] at h -- works now!

For the rw example you might want to make BufferStrategy @[implicit_reducible]. The change between h before and h after is between Vector s.PosPlusOne bufferSize and (BufferStrategy s bufferSize).Update which weren't equal under with_reducible_and_instances.
By the way, for the simp example, you should also make C₁ @[implicit_reducible] instead of using simp to simplify the types (one might even consider it a bug that simp can rewrite in type positions).
I'll try, thanks! Are there any general guidelines around these topics? I'm eager to learn best practices

There's some work in the lean repository to improve the simp situation. The suggestion there seems to be to change the proof to (rfl) for simp lemmas where the equality isn't at instance transparency. You can also use simp -dsimp to stop all simplification on terms that appear in types of later parameters.
